title: Relative clauses: who the caudillo was

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5. They add information about a person or a thing. Here they help you say who a caudillo was, who followed him and what he did.

sections.title: Who and what the caudillo was
rows: un jefe que tenía su propio ejército
*que* + verb: a chief who had his own army
los peones que trabajaban en sus tierras
*que* after a plural noun: the workers who worked on his land
*que* + *lo* + verb: the men who supported him
with commas, *que* (or *quien*) adds extra information about a named person

items.spanish: Los hombres que seguían al caudillo eran sus peones.
items.english: The men who followed the caudillo were his farm workers.

items.spanish: El caudillo daba tierra a los hombres que lo apoyaban.
items.english: The caudillo gave land to the men who supported him.

items.spanish: Rosas, que era hacendado, conocía bien el campo.
items.english: Rosas, who was a landowner, knew the countryside well.

items.spanish: El caudillo, quien tenía mucho carisma, hablaba bien con la gente.
items.english: The caudillo, who had a lot of charisma, spoke well with people.

sections.content: Use *que* for people and things. *Quien* (plural *quienes*) is for people only, and mostly after a comma or a preposition. After a noun with no comma, *que* is the normal choice: *un jefe que tenía*, not *un jefe quien tenía*.
